items.headline: US preparing ordered departure of some Gulf embassy personnel — possible hostilities with Houthis
bullets: State Dept is preparing to issue an ordered departure of some personnel and family members from US embassies across the Gulf, per three US officials (Reuters, Oct 21).
Move tied to a possible resumption of hostilities, particularly with Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen — a fresh escalation signal inside the blockade arc.
No FX repricing yet: DXY +0.07%, EUR/USD -0.15%, USD/JPY +0.06% — noise around covered ranges; oil to watch overnight.

items.headline: NZ CPI misses at 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% expected — takes the edge off the Oct 28 RBNZ hike, Kiwi dipped
bullets: Numbers: Q3 CPI +0.7% q/q vs 0.8% expected, 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% (from 4.1%; RBNZ had projected 3.9%) — petrol -6.5% q/q did the dragging; non-tradables stayed sticky at 1.0% q/q / 3.3% y/y (Stats NZ, official release Oct 22 NZDT).

Read: a soft one-tenth miss on a market ~81% priced for a 25bp RBNZ hike on Oct 28 — it trims the odds without killing the case, and the price action agrees: NZD/USD slipped from just above to just under 0.5700, back where it traded before its five-session climb.
Watch: the Oct 28 RBNZ decision — markets priced 18-21bp before the print; December (+50% odds) is where a softer path would show up first.

items.headline: US Treasury sanctions Karnakis & Karnakis law firm + Iran shadow-fleet network (Operation Economic Outcast)
bullets: OFAC designated Greece/Panama law firm Karnakis & Karnakis, 5 individuals, Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents, and blocked 9 vessels under EO 13902 — accused of concealing Iranian oil, petrochemical and steel shipments (Treasury, Oct 21).
FinCEN issued its first-ever admin subpoena under 31 USC 5318(k) probing a Greek bank's Iran ties, plus info requests to six other European banks over Iran-linked relationships.
Still the enforcement lane, not the strike lane: Reuters notes Washington has 'held off striking Iran this month' and is running the blockade + sanction waves instead — oil price reaction nil so far.
